title: Spartacus
objective: After this level you can describe the slave revolt led by Spartacus and how it ended.
summary: In 73 BCE the gladiator Spartacus led a slave revolt that grew to tens of thousands. Crassus crushed it in 71 BCE.

cards.headline: A gladiator escaped his school and raised an army that shook Rome.
cards.body: It began with a breakout at a gladiator school in Capua. It ended with a road lined with crosses. In between, an army of the enslaved defeated several Roman forces.

cards.headline: The breakout
cards.body: In 73 BCE Spartacus, a gladiator from Thrace, escaped from a gladiator school at Capua and began a slave revolt. Remember those huge estates from Level 31? Their owners’ wealth depended on the enslaved people who worked them. Now those people had a leader. The rebel army grew to tens of thousands and defeated several Roman forces. The workforce had become an army.

cards.headline: A brutal end
cards.body: In 71 BCE the general Marcus Crassus crushed the revolt. Some 6,000 captured rebels were crucified along the Appian Way, the Via Appia you met in Level 19. Rome’s first great road, built to move armies, became a warning lined with crosses. Rome won the war. But Spartacus outlived his defeat, as a lasting symbol of resistance to oppression.

cards.headline: Why Rome was afraid
cards.body: Here’s why a slave army was such a nightmare for Rome’s rich. The great estates of Level 31 were worked by enslaved people, so wealthy fortunes rested on the very people now in revolt. Imagine your whole business running on workers who have walked out and started beating your security guards. That is roughly where Rome’s landowners stood.

cards.headline: The revolt: ended
learned: His revolt began at Capua in 73 BCE

questions.prompt: What was Spartacus before he led the revolt?
questions.explanation: Spartacus was a Thracian gladiator who escaped from a school at Capua.

questions.prompt: Why did the revolt alarm Rome’s wealthy so much?

options.label: Spartacus planned to become king
options.rationale: The fear was economic and social.

options.label: Their estates depended on enslaved workers

questions.explanation: Italy’s great estates were worked by enslaved people, so a slave army threatened the whole system.

questions.prompt: From Level 19: along which road were the captured rebels crucified?
questions.explanation: Crassus lined the Appian Way, Rome’s first great road, with crucified rebels.
